title: Mutual Trim+
tagline: Onshape's mutual trim, with the side to keep on each surface named by a reference instead of by a flip -- so the trim keeps the right corner whatever the surfaces' orientations.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Two surfaces trim each other along their intersection and each keeps one side. The built-in picks that side with a 'keep opposite side' box per surface, tied to each surface's normal -- which flips when a loft, offset or mirror upstream changes. Mutual Trim+ keeps, on each surface, the side a reference is on.
useWhen: Two surfaces meet at a corner you want to keep (a top and a wall)
Either surface's orientation may change upstream
A fillet or thicken will follow the trim edge
slides.caption: Mutual Trim+ open on the ski: unfilleted top x SW rout wall.

slides.title: Why a reference instead of a flip

points.head: A flip is about a normal
points.body: 'Front', 'opposite direction', 'Thickness 1' all mean: relative to the normal -- and normals change freely upstream.

points.head: A reference is about the model
points.body: Pick geometry on the side you mean. The choice survives any change of orientation.

points.head: Drop-in
points.body: With no reference, the feature behaves exactly like the built-in.

points.head: Against the OTHER surface
points.body: Each surface is cut in two by the other one. The side kept is the one on the reference's side of that other surface (signed distance).

points.head: Not by nearness
points.body: On a leaning wall the nearest piece can be the wrong one (right). Distance is only a fallback when the pieces do not straddle the other surface.

points.head: Per surface
points.body: Each surface has its own 'keep side nearest reference' arrow: on = the reference's side, off = the other side.

slides.title: The dialog
params: The arrow by the first surface. On: keep its side nearer the reference (the inside). Off: the farther side.
The same for the second surface.
Geometry on the keep side of BOTH surfaces -- best a mate connector or vertex in the corner you keep. Empty = the built-in.
Union the two trimmed surfaces into one body (default on).
Print side distances: which side each surface kept, and whether by side (normal case) or by distance (fallback).

slides.title: Example: top x sidewall rout
slides.head: Unfilleted_Top_Surf trimmed with SW_Rout, reference Better_Ref, merged (topsheet_surf studio)
slides.body: Each surface keeps the part on the reference's side of the other: the top keeps its inside (green), the rout wall keeps the part below the top (blue). The published trimEdges (magenta) is the intersection along which the two were trimmed -- the edge a fillet wants.

slides.title: Example: the whole trim edge
slides.head: The same result from above: keptFaces1 (green) and the trim edge all round the ski (magenta)
slides.body: keptFaces1 / keptFaces2 tell the two surfaces apart even after Merge makes them one body, so a later feature can offset or thicken just the top, or just the wall.

keys: The trimmed surfaces (one body when merged).
The intersection edges the trim left -- where to fillet. Tracked through the merge.
The faces the first surface kept (still told apart after the merge).
The faces the second surface kept.
messages: The surfaces do not intersect; nothing was trimmed.
The keep side reference cannot be placed on either side of the first/second surface
The pieces do not straddle the other surface and the reference is equally far from both. Pick a closer reference inside the corner to keep.

items.head: Put the reference in the corner you keep
items.body: A mate connector just inside the kept corner (e.g. at MRS) -- not a far plane: a far plane's closest point can land at the tip, where the surfaces have turned.

items.head: Fillet along trimEdges
items.body: Publish trimEdges with Extract variables; it survives upstream edits that renumber edges.

items.head: Outputs keep their input's orientation
items.body: The reference picks the side, not the normal. Built-ins downstream that follow the normal (Thicken, Offset surface, Move face) need Orient to reference first -- or use the reference-side feature instead.

items.head: One orientation after Merge
items.body: Merged, the two halves are one body with one orientation.
